subject: Customer security questionnaire: Hosted API — data residency, retention, and erasure
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya.patel@novacorp.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: security@novacorp.com
Date: Wed, 21 Aug 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Customer security questionnaire: data residency + retention (hosted API)

Hi Dylan,

We're running through the last set of checks before our procurement team signs off. A handful of short questions about Redwood's Hosted API data lifecycle — could you confirm the answers below or point me to a single doc that covers everything? We prefer concise, concrete answers we can include in our supplier security questionnaire.

1) Region/Residency: If we pick US-only, where are request/response payloads and generated artifacts stored? Are backups or logs ever replicated out-of-region by default?

2) Retention windows: What is the default retention for (a) raw request payloads, (b) generated responses, (c) embeddings, (d) telemetry/usage logs, and (e) audit logs? Can we set per-tenant overrides?

3) Deletion/Erasure: If we ask for tenant data erasure, what's the timeline for (a) primary store deletion, (b) backup snapshot purge, and (c) log/analytics deletion? Do you provide an API and an attestation/cert that data was deleted?

4) Backups & Snapshots: How long are backups retained, where are they stored, and are they encrypted with customer-managed keys?

5) Caching: Does the serving runtime use any long-lived prefix/KV caches that could keep customer data beyond standard retention? Can cache be disabled per tenant?

6) Model improvement: Do you use customer request/response data to train or fine-tune models? If so, is that opt-in?

7) Evidence: Can you provide SOC2 or other attestation artifacts and a contact for technical follow-up?

We're trying to close the loop quickly; a one-page matrix or bullet answers are ideal.

Thanks,
Anya
Anya Patel
Senior Security Engineer — NovaCorp

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Patel <anya.patel@novacorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Aug 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Customer security questionnaire: data residency + retention (hosted API)

Anya —

Thanks for the clear list. I'm attaching a short retention/residency matrix and a FAQ that maps questions to policy text. High-level answers inline below; Marissa (security) and Ben (account lead) are looped in for details and contracting. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you prefer.

Quick answers (summary):
- Region/Residency: You can pin to a single region (US West or US East). Primary request/response data and generated artifacts are stored in-region. Backups are encrypted and stored in-region by default; cross-region replication only happens with an explicit enterprise configuration.
- Retention windows: Default hosted settings are: requests/responses 30 days ephemeral, embeddings 90 days (used for embeddings index features when enabled), telemetry/usage logs 365 days, audit logs 7 years (for enterprise customers we can adjust). Per-tenant overrides are supported on Dedicated/Enterprise plans — we'll confirm scope for Hosted.
- Deletion: We expose a tenant-level purge API and will provide an erasure attestation. Primary store marking happens immediately; background purge jobs generally complete within 48 hours. Backups are retained per backup retention policy (default 90 days); we can negotiate shorter windows for enterprise addenda.
- Caching: KV/prefix caches are short TTL by default (1 hour) and can be disabled for your tenant.
- Model improvement: We do not use hosted-customer data to train public models by default. Any use for internal model improvement is strictly opt-in and subject to contract.

Attaching: redwood_data_retention_matrix.pdf, redwood-hosted-data-handling-FAQ.md

Next steps: If you want tighter backup purge windows or customer-managed key options, Ben can open an enterprise addendum and Marissa can provide the SOC2 link and evidence.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Patel <anya.patel@novacorp.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Aug 2029 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Customer security questionnaire: data residency + retention (hosted API) — detailed responses

Hi Anya —

Thanks for the questions. Below are explicit answers you can paste into your questionnaire. I kept them concise and numbered to match your original list. If you need a one-line snippet for procurement, tell me which fields to shorten.

1) Region/Residency:
- Primary storage: When you select US-only, all primary request/response payloads, generated outputs (text, images), and tenant-specific metadata are written to storage within the selected US region (US-West or US-East).
- Backups & replication: By default, point-in-time backups are encrypted and stored in the same region. Cross-region replication is not enabled for standard Hosted customers. Cross-region replication or multi-region geo-redundancy is available only via an explicit enterprise configuration and documented in the addendum.

2) Retention windows (default Hosted policy):
- Raw request payloads (text prompts, files uploaded to the request) — 30 days (ephemeral).
- Generated responses (model outputs returned to the customer) — 30 days (ephemeral).
- Embeddings (if enabled and persisted by customer configuration) — 90 days (used only to power indexing features).
- Telemetry/usage logs (aggregated request metrics for monitoring) — 365 days (retained for product/service analytics).
- Audit logs (security-relevant events, admin actions) — 7 years for enterprise customers; 1 year for standard Hosted by default.

Note: For Hosted customers, per-tenant adjustments to retention (shorter windows) are possible with an enterprise addendum; dedicated instances allow full control.

3) Deletion/Erasure:
- API: We provide a documented Tenant Erasure API endpoint (POST /v1/tenants/{id}/erase) which creates a signed job and returns a job id.
- Primary store: On request, records are marked for immediate deletion; background workers purge reachable data from primary stores within 24–48 hours.
- Backups/snapshots: Backups are immutable snapshots; they are deleted according to retention policy when the snapshot expires. Standard default snapshot purge is 90 days; with an addendum we can reduce this to 45 days. Complete removal from long-term backup media can take up to the negotiated backup retention window.
- Logs/analytics: Aggregated telemetry is purged on the next weekly processing window; detailed audit logs are purged per configured retention window.
- Attestation: We provide deletion attestations (signed PDF) tied to the erase job id upon completion.

4) Backups & Snapshots:
- Retention: Default 90 days for hosted; enterprise customers can negotiate.
- Storage & encryption: Backups stored in-region, encrypted at rest with AES-256. Customer-managed KMS keys (Bring Your Own Key) are available on the Enterprise plan; for Hosted standard, keys are managed by Redwood with strict key-rotation policies.

5) Caching:
- Serving runtime uses short-lived KV/prefix caches to accelerate generation. Default TTL is 1 hour; caches are not used for long-term persistence.
- Cache disabling: Cache layer can be disabled or given a 0s TTL for your tenant upon request.

6) Model improvement:
- Hosted customer data is NOT used to train or fine-tune models unless the customer explicitly opts-in via a documented agreement. Internal product telemetry (non-identifiable usage patterns) may inform product decisions, but we do not feed raw customer prompts/responses into model training without consent.

7) Evidence:
- SOC2 Type II report and security whitepaper: https://redwood.app/security/soc2-report (requires NDA access; Ben will share a secure link).
- Technical contact: marissa_cole@redwood.ai (I can coordinate artifact transfer and evidence kit).

Operational notes:
- We provide a standard SLA-backed erasure workflow for enterprise customers that includes a signed attestation and ticket tracking.
- For low-latency customers that require stricter retention, we recommend a Dedicated deployment or Enterprise addendum that includes BYOK and 45-day snapshot purge.

If you'd like, Ben can start an addendum draft that specifies 45-day backup purge and BYOK.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — security@redwood.ai

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear answers. A couple of quick clarifications before I hand this to procurement:

- When you say backups are "deleted according to retention policy" — does the deletion process ensure restoration from older snapshots is impossible after the snapshot retention window? In other words, can you confirm that after the 90-day (or negotiated 45-day) window, the backup media no longer contains recoverable customer data?

- For debugging safety: If we request an erasure job, do you retain a minimally redacted copy of the original request/response for debugging or support purposes? If yes, what's the retention on that artifact?

- Embeddings: If embeddings are persisted for our tenant, can we request immediate index purge independent of the 90-day default?

We prefer a contractual 45-day backup purge. Procurement will ask for the DocuSign link for the addendum once you confirm you can provide it.

Thanks,
Anya

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Patel <anya.patel@novacorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Aug 2029 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Customer security questionnaire: Hosted API — data residency, retention, and erasure — next steps

Anya —

Short answers to your clarifications and next steps:

- Backup destruction: Yes — when a snapshot reaches end-of-retention it is expired and removed from active backup indices. For cloud object-store based snapshots we delete the metadata and then issue object-store deletion calls; object-store garbage-collection windows may apply but we include the GC window in the negotiated retention. The snapshot deletion workflow is audited and we can provide a signed attestation once the agreed snapshot window elapses.

- Debugging artifacts: We do NOT retain unredacted copies of customer request/response for debugging post-erasure. Support captures are either ephemeral (used only with customer consent during a support session) or are redacted/hashed. Any case where we need a short-term support snapshot is done with customer approval and a defined TTL (default 7 days) and logged in the audit trail.

- Embeddings index purge: Yes — we can purge embeddings/index artifacts on-request independent of backup retention. The purge job will remove entries from the index service and issue a storage reclaim; however, if embeddings were included in backups they will still be removed according to backup retention unless the addendum shortens that window.

Contracting: Ben will open an enterprise addendum that (a) sets backup snapshot purge to 45 days, (b) includes BYOK for backups, and (c) adds the erasure attestation clause. I've attached a placeholder DocuSign link to the draft addendum for procurement to review.

DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.com/example/ds-REDWOOD-ADD-18937
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/18937

If that looks good I can have Legal loop in the final addendum today.

— Dylan
